answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a live utility connection inspected by a licensed electrician outside the farm. One timber pole feeds one address; the inspector certifies the copper wiring and issues one connection certificate per identity — a bridge between the identity and a real billed household. One crew does one site per day, so inspections cannot be bulk-bought or parallelized. Each extra fake needs another real address, another inspection, and an outside-money fee doubling per connection on the same funding trail: the tenth fake costs one more visit plus 512x the first fee.
